0: Feature construction: multiply each nonpadding input item embedding by 1 + 0.1*min(log(c), log(5)), where c is that item's causal occurrence count through the current position in the supplied history window. This deterministic repeat-frequency feature may strengthen recurring interests without new learned embeddings or an independent scorer. Keep SASRec topology, readout, loss and optimizer fixed; apply identical feature construction during prediction.

Greater token-wise nonlinear capacity may improve discrimination among similar candidates. Keep features, embeddings, history selection, scoring, readout, loss and optimizer fixed, and update the predictor writer to reconstruct the same architecture.
2: Sequence modeling: set the maximum causal context length to 100 interactions, retaining the latest interactions in chronological order with the existing padding and positional-encoding convention. This tests whether a bounded recent history improves next-item relevance across the four datasets. Preserve feature definitions, embedding design, SASRec blocks, readout, loss and optimizer; use the identical context rule in training and prediction.
3: Training strategy: retain the baseline optimizer and peak learning rate, but add linear learning-rate warmup over the first 5% of configured epochs followed by cosine decay to 10% of the peak. Smoother early updates and smaller late updates may improve validation ranking. Keep seed 42, the 200-epoch cap, batch size, dropout, weight decay, loss, architecture and evaluation fixed; prediction loads one selected checkpoint per category.
